title: Derby takeover withdrawn after regulatory approval; club returns to current ownership
dek: Saudi Arabia official Turki Alalshikh withdrew his proposed takeover of Championship club Derby County after the deal had been sanctioned by the English Football League and Independent Football Regulator. Alalshikh cited timing pressure tied to the season's start as the reason for the withdrawal.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: The deal with Alalshikh's Lion Sport had been approved by the EFL and IFR before he withdrew on Monday, per BBC Sport and ESPN reporting.
bottom_line: Derby enters the 2026-27 season under existing ownership. Watch whether Alalshikh pursues other club acquisitions or returns to Derby with a revised timeline. The story would shift if disclosure emerged about undisclosed obstacles during the regulatory phase or if financial conditions changed between approval and withdrawal.
body: Saudi Arabia official and boxing promoter Turki Alalshikh withdrew his proposed takeover of Championship club Derby County on Monday after regulatory approval had already been secured, according to BBC Sport and ESPN reporting. The deal with Alalshikh's Lion Sport had been sanctioned by the English Football League and the Independent Football Regulator before the withdrawal.

Alalshikh framed the withdrawal as a consequence of timeline pressure introduced by the season's start. He stated on social media, per BBC Sport: "We understood that the IFR process takes time and fully respect the importance of that. But unfortunately with the season already started, it would leave us with no time to prepare the team or the club for the season ahead. After careful consideration, we don't feel it is right to proceed at this time without the necessary preparation in place." He added that he would remain in conversation with the club regarding future possibilities.

The Independent Football Regulator reached a "minded-to decision" to approve the bid in 55 days out of the 90 days allowed by law, according to ESPN. The IFR had communicated this decision to all parties last week, before the 2026-27 season began. The regulator assesses all prospective owners against tests on financial soundness, sufficient financial resources, source of wealth, and honesty and integrity, including checks on criminal proceedings, convictions, civil actions and regulatory investigations, per ESPN's reporting.

Derby released a statement confirming the club's return to existing stewardship: "For the benefit of any doubt, the club is now off the market. It will continue to operate under the loyal, committed and unwavering support of Clowes Developments." The club begins its league campaign at Charlton on Saturday, per ESPN.
The withdrawal came despite all regulatory hurdles having been cleared, making it a rare instance of a deal collapsing at the finish line rather than during the approval process itself.
